record.paper_title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can graphical causal methods be explicitly integrated with multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), where multiple learning agents interact in a shared environment, so that causal reinforcement-learning methods that already support off-policy learning, data fusion, and counterfactual reasoning can address the additional complexities introduced by interacting agents?

evidence.quote: This has been attempted with speciﬁc tasks in mind, such as off-policy learning (Buesing et al., 2018), data-fusion (Bareinboim and Pearl, 2016; Gasse et al., 2021; Forney et al., 2017), and counterfactual reasoning (Forney and Bareinboim, 2019). This paper considers extending causal RL methods to the multi-agent case, where additional complexities arise due to interacting agents.

While there has been some interest in merging ideas from causality with current single-agent methods, to the best of our knowledge no research explicitly looks at bridging (graphical) causal methods with MARL.
It is our belief that causal methods are especially well suited for dealing with the additional challenges and complexity in multi-agent problems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) setting formalized as a Markov game (S, {A_i}_{i=1}^n, P, {R_i}_{i=1}^n, γ), in which n agents simultaneously choose actions a_i ∈ A_i in state s ∈ S, the environment transitions according to P(s' | s, a_1, …, a_n), and each agent i receives reward R_i(s, a_1, …, a_n, s') and seeks to maximize its discounted return E[Σ_t γ^t R_i,t]. Augment this setting with a structural causal model (SCM) M = (U, V, F, P(U)) whose endogenous variables V include the states, the joint actions, and the rewards across time, whose exogenous variables U represent unobserved confounders that may simultaneously influence multiple agents' policies and the environment, and whose structural equations F induce a causal graph G over V.

Develop a unified framework that explicitly integrates graphical causal inference (interventions do(·), counterfactuals, identifiability of causal effects from observational and interventional data via the do-calculus, and data fusion across heterogeneous sources) with MARL, such that the following are simultaneously addressed:

(1) Off-policy evaluation and learning: given trajectories generated by behavior joint policies that may differ from the target joint policies and that may be confounded by U, derive estimators of each agent's target-policy value that are consistent under the causal graph G.

(2) Data fusion: given a collection of datasets D_1, …, D_k arising from different experimental or observational regimes (e.g., interventions on subsets of agents, partial observability, simulator vs. real environment), give graphical conditions on G under which the joint-policy value or per-agent counterfactual quantities are identifiable from {D_j} and provide an algorithm to compute them.

(3) Counterfactual reasoning with interacting agents: define and identify counterfactual best-response and counterfactual regret quantities of the form E[R_i(s, a_1, …, a_{i-1}, a'_i, a_{i+1}, …, a_n) | observed trajectory] in the presence of unobserved confounders shared across agents, and characterize when such quantities are identifiable from available data.

State and prove identifiability theorems and provide provably convergent learning algorithms that solve (1)–(3) jointly in the n ≥ 2 agent case, recovering known single-agent causal RL results in the limit n = 1.
artifact.status_search_result: The integration of graphical causal inference with multi-agent reinforcement learning remains an active and largely open research program. While individual components (off-policy evaluation, counterfactual policy evaluation, and data fusion) have been studied in single-agent causal RL, no comprehensive framework providing identifiability theorems and convergent algorithms for the full multi-agent case has been established as of the search date. Recent works explore pieces of the problem (e.g., causal influence in MARL, counterfactual credit assignment), but the overall problem of explicitly bridging graphical causal methods with MARL is acknowledged as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey explicitly framing the bridging of graphical causal methods with MARL as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The unified integration of graphical causal methods with MARL is identified as an open research direction.
